title: Two Pawns, One Diagonal
setup: You are far behind on material and your own king has been chased to d2, but the black king is walled in by its own pieces.
hint: Start by counting the black king's squares rather than your material — then ask what the pawn on b7 is really holding.
explanation:
## The Idea

The king on c8 has no square: d8, d7 and b7 hold its own rook, knight and pawn, and the bishop on f4 covers c7 and b8. Only the pawn on b7 keeps your other bishop off a6.

{{Qxc6+}} gives the queen for a pawn, and {{bxc6}} is Black's only legal move. The pawn has left b7, and {{Ba6#}} lands on the square it used to guard.

Count the enemy king's squares before you count material, and a queen becomes something you can spend.
